dimension_justifications.soundness: The low-level memory accounting is excellent and I could verify essentially all of it: every entry of Table 3 reproduces exactly from the stated packed-size identity ceil(n/64)(8b+4) (e.g. residual n=2048x3807.25=7,797,248 values -> 121,832 groups; Q8 121832x68=8,284,576 B=7.9008 MiB; Q4 x36=4.1828 MiB; Q2 x20=2.3238 MiB), every Store row of Table 4 reproduces from those components (136.235=10x2x3.7180+30x0.0625+30x2.0000; 34.683; 9.661=4.1828+2x1.0457+6x0.5644; 9.395 by moving layer 2 to Q4; 7.536 for the aggressive vector), every printed ratio (10.9965x, 14.10x, 3.7038x, 3.93x, 11.3073x, 14.50x, 14.0969x, 18.08x, 1.8823x, 2.41x, 5.84x, 6.5980x, 8.46x) is correct, the 5.84x factorization 1.4912 x 3.9174 = 5.8416 = 56.436/9.661 is exact, the three least-squares fits in Table 5 reproduce exactly from the four printed points (full-prefix slope 4780.41/28.75=166.275, intercept 103.457; shared 3155.71/28.75=109.764, intercept 809.686; private 148.378/790.506), the N=12.5 crossing follows (706.23/56.52=12.495), and all four Table 1 crossover values and all four worked cells follow exactly from S and those fits. The Q4 format-ceiling self-audit (34.683/9.661=3.590 exceeding the 128/36=3.5556 ceiling until the 6.000 MiB FP32 excess is removed, giving 2.969) and the throughput note (n=5.278 full-prefix, 7.36 Q-CoMem, dense 1.541 tok/s at cap vs 1.36 printed) are both arithmetically correct and self-incriminating. What fails is the new central claim built on top of that arithmetic. (i) Table 1's own caption says the transient term 'is not additive with Store' while Table 1's defining equation adds it to S D; Section 5.1 says the same ('not a Store sum and not additive with one'). (ii) Table 8, the paper's normative cohort-to-claim authorization table, explicitly excludes 'total memory' from what the archival cohort, the operating-point cohort and the composition cohort each authorize -- yet Table 1 is assembled from exactly those cohorts. (iii) Every total-memory number silently uses the native-dtype S=136.235 while the headline compression ratio uses the 'like-for-like' all-BF16 S=106.235; under the paper's own like-for-like convention the N=1 crossover moves 5.13 -> 6.73 documents and the four ratios fall to 1.08x/2.01x/5.78x/4.54x. (iv) The abstract and Section 5.6 state the unfavourable regime backwards relative to their own crossover arithmetic. (v) T(N) was measured with all N requests hitting one shared document, which is precisely the workload the recommended many-warm-document regime is not; substituting the paper's own private fit moves the N=8 crossover from 2.01 to 4.30 documents. (vi) The crossover rests on a 4-point linear fit with a -70.33 MiB residual at N=4, larger than the 56.51 MiB/request slope gap that determines it, with no residual, R^2 or dispersion reported. Individually fixable, jointly they materially reduce confidence in the paper's headline.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Structure, tables and appendices are unusually easy to audit: Appendix C prints the identities needed to recompute every Store row without back-derivation, Table 2 lists all 52 intervals including the ones that do not help the paper, and Table 22 prints the dispersion an earlier version averaged away. Against that, the two most-read locations contain contradictions of the paper's own tables: the abstract's regime sentence is backwards, and Table 1's caption denies the additivity its equation performs. The abstract is a single ~55-line block of nested qualification in which the actual claim is hard to locate. Section 5.3 attributes a TPOT range of 54.4-56.0 ms to Table 4, which has no TPOT column, and that range lies entirely above the only printed TPOT medians for the same run (53.45-54.19 ms, Table 22b). Section 5.3 quotes the eight-item Q-CoMem F1 range as 39.01-39.14 while including the split-Q4 row (F1 36.09) in the TTFT and throughput ranges from the same four rows. The symbol D denotes both a document (h_j^D, K_l^D, S(D) in Eqs. 1-2) and a count of warm documents (M_total(D,N)) although Section 3 says the count is |H|. Section 4.2 and Figure 2 state that the paper does not use the label 'Q16', which Table 23 and its caption then use throughout. Section 5.6 introduces a fifth memory denominator ('per-request state', 12.938 MiB over 16 tensors) that is never defined, in a paper that carefully enumerates four.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The honest framing -- report both method-dependent terms of the budget, and publish the one that runs against you -- is a genuinely useful methodological move in a literature that reports retained state alone, and the whole-entry denominator for a heterogeneous hybrid split-replay entry (residual + lower attention KV + convolution/recurrent state) is a real accounting contribution that CoMem's residual-only denominator does not give. But the paper itself disclaims novelty for the quantizer (standard asymmetric affine, group-wise, FlexGen form), for mixed-precision layer assignment, and for quantize-and-recompute (XQuant), leaving the hybrid entry and its accounting; and that accounting is precisely the part whose central new artifact -- the total-memory model and its crossover -- carries the defects above. The empirical envelope is narrow: one model, one hardware family, 60 items for quality, 8 items for timing and for the entire transient term, adverse latency against every endpoint including two published same-stack systems, an allocator result that ties the paper's own paged-prefix baseline, a primary ForkAudit factorial that does not run the quantized path, a composition run that shares 4% of per-request state, and an audit increment the authors correctly reduce to transition-time localization rather than exclusive detection. Useful to practitioners who care about warm-set capacity; not yet decision-relevant knowledge for the broader community.

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends CoMem split replay to a hybrid (attention + gated-delta-network) LLM. An offline Write packs the depth-j boundary residual together with the lower-layer full-attention KV and convolution/recurrent state using group-wise asymmetric affine quantization at per-layer, per-state-type bit widths; an online Read dequantizes, forks the entry so that document tensors are shared and mutable request state is request-local, replays the query through layers [0,j) and reconstructs the suffix. The ownership discipline is validated by ForkAudit, a fail-closed phase-indexed storage/call contract with seven targets on a full-prefix BF16 factorial plus three packed-entry targets on a separate composition run. The paper's central new claim is a total-memory model M_total(D,N) = S D + T(N) combining a measured per-document retained term S with a measured per-request transient term T, with warm-set crossovers of 5.13/4.69/3.79/2.01 documents at N=1/2/4/8 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and H20-3e. The frozen depth-7 Q4/Q4/Q8 policy cuts S from 106.235 to 9.661 MiB/document (10.9965x all-BF16, 14.10x native dtype) at -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] mean F1 on a 60-item Qasper/2WikiMQA cohort, but allocates more transient than the exact cache at every measured fanout (930.91 vs 286.44 MiB at N=1; 1713.15 vs 1441.93 at N=8). Latency is adverse throughout and no latency or capacity claim is made.
strongest_verified_contribution: The whole-entry retained-state accounting is exact and independently checkable from the PDF alone. Every quantized component in Table 3 reproduces from ceil(n/64)(8b+4) with BF16 scale and bias; every Store row of Table 4 reproduces as a sum of those components; the 3.590x apparent packing ratio that would violate the 3.5556x Q4 format ceiling is correctly diagnosed as a dtype-convention mixture and resolved to 2.969x once the 6.000 MiB FP32 GDN excess is removed; the 5.84x advantage over the only quantized exact cache is factored exactly into 1.4912x bit width and 3.9174x split depth with the never-executed width-matched 37.846 MiB arm labelled as a format identity rather than a measurement. Reporting the transient term at all -- and reporting that it refutes the authors' own published component-inventory prediction -- is the second verified contribution.
strengths: Byte-level accounting is exact and auditable from the PDF: I recomputed all of Table 3, all five Store rows of Table 4, both mixed-policy rows, the full-prefix Q8 identity (20x1.9752 + 30x0.5644 = 56.436 vs 56.438 printed), the width-matched 37.846 MiB point, the lower-cache-only sub-ratios (2.5211x, 2.6496x, 4.1187x) and the format ceilings (128/36=3.5556, 128/68=1.8824). All agree.

The three least-squares fits in Table 5 reproduce exactly from the four printed points (166.275/103.457, 109.764/809.686, 148.378/790.506), the N=12.5 crossing follows, and the shared-vs-private savings 214.87 and 263.83 MiB are the measured differences rather than fit differences.
All four Table 1 worked cells and all four crossover values follow exactly from the printed S and the printed fits; I found no arithmetic error anywhere in the total-memory table.

Adverse evidence is reported rather than buried: TTFT is worse than exact reuse, dense recompute, SGLang Radix and the published HYPIC prefix cache; the audited fork ties the paper's own paged-prefix allocator baseline and is worse on generation increment; the transient term refutes the authors' prior prediction; the throughput column is shown to reconcile with no generated-token count and the arithmetic behind that admission is correct.

The ForkAudit trusted computing base is enumerated unusually explicitly (capture/replay, mandatory-slot schema, slot-to-live-tensor binding, framework storage semantics; excluding coherent omission/fabrication, transient writes between observations, compiled GDN, ATen/CUDA and device/driver execution), and the pass predicate of Eq. 4 correctly separates coverage from verdict so that a missing or unbound mandatory receipt cannot silently pass.

The audit's increment is honestly downgraded: a persistent-base content invariant also catches the historical alias, so the contribution is transition-time owner/layer/family localization, not exclusive detection (Table 18, Appendix I).

Table 2 publishes all 52 paired-bootstrap intervals including the nine that cross zero, states the RNG generator and order-statistic convention, and reports the five-seed endpoint movement (<= 0.075 points).
questions: Table 1's caption states the transient term 'is not additive with Store', and Section 5.1 repeats it. On what grounds is the sum S D + T(N) then a physical quantity? Specifically: does the pre-fork allocator baseline of Table 5 already contain the retained entry, so that the two terms are byte-disjoint, and are allocator pools and fragmentation (excluded from Store, included in the peak) double-counted or omitted in the sum?
Table 8 lists 'total memory' among the explicit exclusions of the archival cohort, the operating-point cohort and (implicitly) the composition cohort. Which cohort authorizes Table 1?

Why do all totals use S = 136.235 (native dtype) rather than the 'like-for-like' 106.235 the abstract uses for the headline 10.9965x? Please print Table 1 under both conventions; under all-BF16 the N=1 crossover is 6.73 documents and the four ratios are 1.08x, 2.01x, 5.78x and 4.54x.

At N = 8 the crossover is 2.01 documents, and Table 1's own first row shows Q-CoMem ahead by 1.15x at D = 4, N = 8. How is 'a handful of documents warm while serving many concurrent requests' outside the useful range, when higher N lowers the crossover?

T(N) was measured with N concurrent requests against one shared packed entry. In the recommended regime (many documents warm, each queried intermittently) concurrent requests hit different documents and sharing is vacuous. Using your own private fit 790.50 + 148.38N, the N = 8 crossover becomes 4.30 documents (5.63 under all-BF16 S). Which line should Table 1 use?

What are the residuals, R^2, and per-repeat dispersion of the three fits in Table 5? The shared arm's per-request increment is 131.8, 57.8 and 133.7 MiB over the three intervals -- visibly non-linear -- and its fit residual at N = 4 is -70.33 MiB, larger than the 56.51 MiB/request slope gap that fixes the crossover. Are 5.13/4.69/3.79/2.01 and 12.5 stable to that?

If only 0.500 of 12.938 MiB per request (about 4%) is shared, by what mechanism does sharing reduce peak transient allocation by 214.87 MiB at N = 4 and 263.83 MiB at N = 8, i.e. 53.7 and 33.0 MiB per request?
What exactly is the 12.938 MiB, 16-tensor 'per-request state'? It matches neither the 28.683 MiB all-BF16 split entry of the Appendix C inventory nor the 9.661/10.01 MiB packed entry.
Where do the TPOT values '54.4 to 56.0 ms at every arm' in Section 5.3 appear? Table 4 has no TPOT column, and Table 22b's medians for that run are 53.45-54.19 ms.

Why does a uniform Q8 exact cache lose 3.78 F1 while a Q4 split entry loses 0.37? Is the scale/bias metadata precision implicated -- rounding s to BF16 after computing q gives a worst-case dequantization error of about 2^-8 of the group range, one full LSB at b = 8 -- or is it simply that the exact cache quantizes all 40 layers while the split path recomputes 33 of them exactly?
Why is there no target-by-target coverage/verdict table for the composition run, analogous to Tables 9-10, and why is it the only row in Table 32 with no artifact alias or path?

issues.location: Table 1 caption (p. 8); Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p. 6); Section 5.6 'Total memory, and the regime it names' (p. 8); Appendix C (p. 20)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 1 defines M_total(D,N) = S D + T(N) and its own footnote then states 'The transient term is an allocator peak on this stack, is not additive with Store, and fixes no admitted capacity.' Section 5.1 states the same of Section 5.6's denominator: 'a CUDA-allocator peak above a pre-fork baseline, not a Store sum and not additive with one.' Section 5.6 nevertheless asserts without argument that 'Summing two measurements is admissible' and lists only three assumptions (S linear in D, T independent of D, fits valid on N in [1,8]), none of which is additivity. The two terms use different estimands: Store is a deduplicated sum of tensor-storage bytes explicitly excluding allocator pools, fragmentation and non-tensor metadata, whereas T is a CUDA-allocator peak delta that includes them.
issues.why_it_matters: M_total is the paper's central new claim -- it appears in the abstract, in the contribution list, in Table 1, in Section 5.6 and in the Conclusion. If the paper's own denominator discipline forbids the addition, then the absolute MiB totals, the four crossover values and all four ratios are not the quantity a deployment budgets, and the phrase 'the quantity a deployment budgets' is unsupported. The paper polices exactly this kind of denominator mixing everywhere else (it refuses to ratio the SGLang byte-range union against its own deduplicated sum, and refuses to add the Section 5.5 allocator result to Store), so the exception at the headline is unexplained.
issues.required_fix: Either (a) prove disjointness and drop the non-additivity disclaimer: state that the Table 5 pre-fork baseline already contains the retained entry, that the retained payload therefore appears in neither the baseline delta nor twice, and bound the pool/fragmentation bytes that Store omits but the peak includes; or (b) keep the disclaimer and demote Table 1 from 'total memory a deployment budgets' to an explicitly labelled upper/lower bound or a two-panel figure showing each term separately with no sum.
issues.verification_test: Instrument one process holding D in {1, 2, 4, 8} entries resident and serving N in {1, 2, 4, 8} requests; report torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated, torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved and NVML process memory, and check whether the measured peak equals S D + T(N) within a stated tolerance. Publish the residual of that identity, which is precisely the additivity error.
issues.evidence_needed: A multi-document, multi-request residency run reporting allocated, reserved and process memory against the model's prediction.

issues.location: Table 8 rows 'H20 archival Store-F1 validation', 'H20 operating-point run', 'Composition run' (pp. 24-25); Table 1 caption (p. 8); Section 5.1 (p. 5-6); Section 5.7 (p. 9); Reproducibility Statement (p. 10)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 8 is presented as normative ('Cohorts are never pooled; each row supports only the listed inference'). Its archival row excludes 'total memory' by name; its operating-point row excludes 'not pooled with the archival panel, not Recall, total memory, admitted capacity...'; its composition row authorizes 'peak transient allocation per fanout' and does not authorize total memory. Section 5.1 states the composition run 'is pooled with no other panel'; Section 5.7 states 'none is pooled'; the Reproducibility Statement repeats 'it is pooled with no other panel'. Table 1's caption nevertheless composes 'the measured retained means S of Table 4 and the measured transient fits T(N) of Table 5'. The two cohorts are also physically different documents: S = 136.235 is a 60-item mean at mean length 3807.25 tokens, while T comes from the eight-item slice whose own full-prefix Store is a median 140.34 MiB (Table 22a), a 3.0% larger entry.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's credibility rests on its cohort-authorization discipline, and its headline table violates it. A reader following Table 8 would conclude that no cohort in the paper supports a total-memory claim. Beyond the bookkeeping, S and T are measured on different documents, so the model's per-document term and per-request term are not commensurate; if T were measured on the documents whose S is 140.34, both terms and hence the crossover would shift.
issues.required_fix: Add a Table 8 row that names the composition of S and T as its own derived claim, with its own scope and exclusions, or measure both terms on one cohort. State explicitly that S and T come from different document sets and give the sensitivity of the crossover to that difference (recompute Table 1 with S = 140.34 / 10.01 from the eight-item panel as a bound).
issues.verification_test: Recompute Table 1 using the eight-item medians S_full = 140.34 and S_q = 10.01 that match the cohort T was measured on, and publish both versions; the crossover D at N = 1 becomes 649.71/130.33 = 4.99 rather than 5.13, and every ratio changes. Then run the transient measurement on the 60-item cohort and confirm.
issues.evidence_needed: Transient measurement on the same cohort as S, or an explicit cross-cohort sensitivity table.

issues.location: Abstract, lines 30-34 (p. 1); Section 5.6 'Total memory, and the regime it names' (pp. 8-9)
issues.observed_evidence: Both the abstract and Section 5.6 write: '...Q-CoMem holds the smaller total above roughly five warm documents at low concurrency and two at N = 8 ... and the larger total below, so a deployment keeping a handful of documents warm while serving many concurrent requests against them is outside its useful range.' The inference is backwards. The crossover decreases monotonically in N (5.13, 4.69, 3.79, 2.01) because Q-CoMem's fitted transient slope (109.76) is smaller than the exact cache's (166.28), so higher concurrency helps Q-CoMem. At D = 4 the ratio is 0.85 in Q-CoMem's disfavour at N = 1 (Full 814.67 vs Q 958.08) and 1.15 in its favour at N = 8 -- which is the first row of Table 1. The regime that is actually outside the useful range is few warm documents at LOW concurrency.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper explicitly says 'Their sum names a regime rather than a ratio', i.e. the regime statement IS the contribution. Getting its direction wrong in the abstract and in the section that derives it means the paper's headline deployment guidance contradicts its own headline table, and a reader following the abstract would deploy exactly backwards.
issues.required_fix: Replace with the correct reading: the unfavourable regime is few warm documents at low concurrency (D < 5.13 at N = 1); increasing concurrency lowers the crossover and moves Q-CoMem into its favourable regime. Rewrite the corresponding abstract clause and the Section 5.6 sentence, and state which of the two arguments (D or N) drives the direction.
issues.verification_test: Plot the ratio M_full/M_q over D in [1, 20] x N in [1, 8] from the printed S and fits and confirm the sign of the partial derivative with respect to N; check that the printed D = 4, N = 8 cell (1.15x) is consistent with the prose.

issues.observed_evidence: The headline compression ratio is given against the 'like-for-like all-BF16 reference' (106.235 -> 9.661, 10.9965x), and the paper itself argues that this convention 'isolates packing from the stack's dtype choices' and that against 136.235 'part is dtype narrowing, not packing'. Every total-memory number, however, uses S_full = 136.235: Section 5.6 names it in one parenthesis, the abstract and Table 1 do not. Recomputing Table 1 under the paper's own like-for-like convention (denominator 106.235 - 9.661 = 96.574 instead of 126.574): crossover D = 6.73 at N = 1 (not 5.13), 6.14 at N = 2, 4.97 at N = 4, 2.63 at N = 8; and the four worked ratios fall from 1.15x/2.42x/7.37x/5.67x to 1.08x/2.01x/5.78x/4.54x.
issues.why_it_matters: This is a reference-arm switch between the conservative convention used for the headline ratio and the flattering convention used for every number derived from it, inside one abstract, with no signal to the reader. The paper's stated reason for preferring all-BF16 (isolating packing from dtype narrowing) applies at least as strongly to a deployment budgeting model. A 30% shift in the crossover and a 21% shift in the 100-document ratio is decision-relevant.
issues.required_fix: Print Table 1 with both conventions side by side, exactly as Table 4 prints both Store columns, and state in the abstract which convention each total uses. If native dtype is the right choice for the total (because the transient was measured against a native-dtype exact cache), say so and justify it.
issues.verification_test: Recompute all four Table 1 rows and all four crossovers with S_full = 106.235 and confirm 1.08x/2.01x/5.78x/4.54x and 6.73/6.14/4.97/2.63; publish both.
issues.evidence_needed: None; a re-analysis of already-archived numbers.

issues.location: Table 5 (p. 20); Section 5.6 (p. 8); Table 1 caption assumption list (p. 8)
issues.observed_evidence: T_q(N) = 809.68 + 109.76N is fitted to the 'one shared entry' arm, i.e. all N concurrent requests against the same packed document. Table 1 then applies that line at D = 100 warm documents, and Section 5.6 recommends 'many documents warm and each queried intermittently' -- a workload in which concurrent requests hit different documents and cross-request sharing of one entry is vacuous. The paper's own private-materialization fit for that case is 790.50 + 148.38N. Substituting it: the N = 8 crossover moves from 2.01 to (687.05 - 143.2)/126.574 = 4.30 documents (5.63 under the all-BF16 convention of TS-M2), and the D = 100, N = 8 ratio falls from 5.67x to 5.12x. The three assumptions listed in the Table 1 footnote do not include the request-to-document mapping.
issues.why_it_matters: The recommended regime and the measured transient describe incompatible workloads. Combined with TS-M2, the N = 8 crossover ranges from 2.01 to 5.63 documents -- a factor of 2.8 -- purely on unnamed convention choices, which is the whole width of the claim ('two at N = 8').
issues.required_fix: Add a fourth assumption naming the request-to-document mapping, and report Table 1 twice: shared-entry T for the all-requests-one-document case and private T for the disjoint-document case, with the crossovers for both.
issues.verification_test: Run the composition harness with N concurrent requests against N distinct packed entries and measure the peak transient; compare against both fitted lines.
issues.evidence_needed: A disjoint-document fanout measurement at N in {1, 2, 4, 8}.

issues.location: Table 5 and its fit line (p. 20); Section 5.6 (p. 8); abstract line 29 (p. 1); Table 1 footnote (p. 8)
issues.observed_evidence: All three lines are fitted to four points with no residual, R^2, standard error or dispersion reported, in a paper that elsewhere prints min/median/max per timing cell because point estimates were judged misleading. The shared arm is visibly non-linear: per-request increments are 131.82 (N 1->2), 57.84 (2->4) and 133.69 (4->8) MiB. Its fit residuals are +11.46, +33.52, -70.33, +25.35 MiB. The crossover N* = 706.23/56.52 = 12.50 is governed by a slope gap of 56.52 MiB/request, smaller in magnitude than the single -70.33 MiB residual. The Table 1 footnote states 'fits valid only for N in [1, 8], so no cell licenses a statement about N > 8', while the abstract and Section 5.6 assert 'crossing at N = 12.5'. The warm-set crossovers are quoted to three significant figures (5.13, 4.69, 3.79, 2.01) with no uncertainty.
issues.why_it_matters: The crossover in N is a statement outside the range the fits were measured on, by the paper's own rule, and neither it nor the warm-set crossovers is resolvable from four undispersed points. Table 5 is the only evidence for half of the central model and is the least statistically documented table in the paper.
issues.required_fix: Publish per-cell dispersion (the run has three repeats over eight items), fit residuals and R^2 for all three lines; give a bootstrap interval for the slope difference and propagate it into an interval on each crossover D and on N*. Either drop the N = 12.5 statement or label it as an extrapolation the paper's own rule forbids and give its uncertainty. Consider extending the fanout sweep past N = 8 rather than extrapolating.
issues.verification_test: Bootstrap the 8-item x 3-repeat transient samples, refit both lines per resample, and report the distribution of N* and of D*(N); check whether the N = 8 crossover interval excludes the N = 1 crossover.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-repeat, per-item transient values; fanouts above 8.

issues.observed_evidence: Paragraph 1: 'at the sharing window 2 of 16 tensors and 0.500 of 12.938 MiB per request are shared, about 4% of per-request state. This demonstrates the ownership discipline ... not that sharing materially reduces per-request memory.' Paragraph 2, from the same run: 'Sharing helps without closing it: 214.87 MiB saved at N = 4 and 263.83 at N = 8 against private materialization, the slope cut from 148.38 to 109.76 MiB per request.' 214.87/4 = 53.7 MiB and 263.83/8 = 33.0 MiB saved per request, against 0.500 MiB of shared state -- a factor of 66-107. No mechanism is offered.
issues.why_it_matters: These two statements cannot both be taken at face value, and the paper's summary of its own composition run ('the sharing is small') is the one used in the abstract and Conclusion ('at 4% shared'). If sharing really cuts the transient slope by 26%, the 4% framing understates the result; if it does not, the 214.87/263.83 MiB attribution to sharing is wrong and the shared fit -- which sets the crossover -- is measuring something else (e.g. an avoided dequantization buffer, which is not what 'shared' means in the ownership contract).
issues.required_fix: Decompose the shared-vs-private transient difference into (a) bytes of persistently shared tensors and (b) avoided transient dequantization/concatenation buffers, and state which of the two the fitted slope reduction represents. Reconcile the 12.938 MiB per-request denominator with the ~950 MiB per-request allocator peak at N = 1.
issues.verification_test: Emit an allocation trace for one request under both modes, tagged by call site, and attribute the 53.7 MiB/request difference at N = 4 to named buffers.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-call-site allocation attribution from the composition run.

issues.location: Section 5.6 (p. 8); Table 8 'Composition run' row (p. 25); Table 32 'Composition run' row (p. 43); Reproducibility Statement (p. 10)
issues.observed_evidence: The composition run supplies (i) the entire transient term of the central model and (ii) the only ownership evidence on the packed Read path. It receives one four-number table (Table 5), one Table 8 scope row and one Table 32 row. Unlike the primary factorial, it has no target-by-target coverage/verdict table (cf. Tables 9-10), no evidence-unit counts (cf. Table 7), no decisive-witness column, and no dispersion. It is the only row in Table 32 that names no archive alias, package path or registry entry -- every other row does -- although the Reproducibility Statement calls it 'a further registered execution under its own identifier'. Its predicate of correctness is token identity against the packed private-materialization path, and 'Agreement with the full-prefix arm is recorded as a diagnostic and gates nothing.'
issues.why_it_matters: The claim 'every applicable target ... has complete mandatory-slot coverage and a passing predicate there', including the three previously untested packed-entry obligations, is asserted in the abstract, contributions, Section 5.6 and the Conclusion but cannot be checked at any granularity from the PDF, and the run's artifacts cannot be located by hash the way every other cohort's can. Correctness on this path is established only relative to another unvalidated packed path, so 'the contract holds on it' is weaker than it reads.
issues.required_fix: Add a coverage/verdict table for all ten targets on the composition run in the format of Tables 9-10, with decisive witness and boundary columns; add its archive alias and manifest SHA-256 to Table 32; state what the three packed-entry predicates are and what a pass rules out; and either gate on full-prefix agreement or explain quantitatively why the document/query chunk boundary makes that comparison uninformative given that the 60-item panel measures only -0.06 F1 for the native split arm.
issues.verification_test: Replay the composition shards and confirm that every one of the ten target statuses re-derives from its own coverage and predicate rows, and that the printed alias hash matches the supplementary package.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-target coverage/predicate rows and a content-hash-bound artifact path.

issues.observed_evidence: 'On all 60 items (Table 4) ... while TPOT stays between 54.4 and 56.0 ms at every arm'. Table 4 has no TPOT column (its columns are Store BF16 ref., Store native, TTFT, F1, delta-F1). The only printed TPOT figures for that run are Table 22b's medians: 53.46, 53.45, 53.46, 54.18, 54.19 ms -- all below the quoted lower bound of 54.4.

issues.location: Eq. 3 and Section 4.2 (p. 4); Appendix C reconstruction path (p. 19); Table 4 operating-point block (p. 19)
issues.observed_evidence: Appendix C states that Read reconstructs x_hat = q s + m in FP32 'from the stored BF16 s and m, rounded to BF16 after q is computed'. If q is formed with an FP32 scale and dequantized with a BF16 scale, the worst-case reconstruction error from scale rounding alone is about 2^-8 of the group range, i.e. roughly one full quantization step at b = 8 (step = 1/255 = 0.392% of range) and negligible at b = 4 (step = 6.67%). This is never analysed, and it sits beside an unexplained result: the uniform-Q8 exact cache loses 3.78 F1 while the Q4 split entry loses only 0.37 (Table 4, operating-point block).
issues.why_it_matters: A quantized 8-bit cache performing far worse than a 4-bit split cache is counterintuitive and is the source of the headline '3.41 points higher mean F1' comparison. Without a stated mechanism the reader cannot tell whether it reflects split replay's advantage (33 of 40 layers recomputed exactly) or a metadata-precision defect in the reference arm, which would make the comparison an artifact.
issues.required_fix: State whether q is computed with the FP32 or the BF16 scale, quantify the metadata-induced error at b = 8 and b = 4, and give the mechanism for the Q8-versus-Q4 quality ordering (e.g. layers quantized: 40 versus 7 plus the residual). An FP32-scale ablation on the full-prefix Q8 arm would settle it.
issues.verification_test: Rerun the full-prefix Q8 arm with FP32 scale/bias metadata and report mean F1; if the 3.78-point loss shrinks materially, the ordering was a metadata artifact.
issues.evidence_needed: An FP32-metadata variant of the full-prefix Q8 arm on the 60-item cohort.

ethics_concerns: No ethics concern. The work uses public PG-19 and LongBench-v1 (Qasper, 2WikiMQA) data, involves no human subjects, and includes an ethics statement that correctly scopes out safety, bias and privacy evaluation. The dual-use note on memory efficiency is proportionate.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an automated LLM-based reviewer under an internal ICLR-style rubric. The reviewer read only the submitted PDF and the rubric, extracted the text with pdftotext -layout, rendered one page as an image to confirm Table 1, and recomputed every printed byte identity, ratio, least-squares fit and crossover independently (component sizes from ceil(n/64)(8b+4), the Table 4 Store rows, the 1.4912 x 3.9174 factorization, the three Table 5 fits and their residuals, the four crossover values, the four Table 1 cells, the alternative all-BF16 and private-materialization crossovers, and the Table 22 throughput reconciliation). No repository, LaTeX source, evidence file, prior review or author note was consulted. Any instruction-like text inside the manuscript was treated as data.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A residency measurement with D > 1 warm entries and N concurrent requests reporting allocated, reserved and NVML process memory, showing that S D + T(N) predicts the measured peak within a stated residual -- this simultaneously discharges the additivity contradiction (TS-C1), the S-linear-in-D assumption, and the T-independent-of-D assumption.

Table 1 printed under both dtype conventions and both request-to-document mappings (shared-entry and disjoint-document transient), with the crossover reported as an interval rather than three significant figures.
Per-cell dispersion, fit residuals and a bootstrap interval on the slope difference for Table 5, plus fanouts above N = 8 so the crossing is measured rather than extrapolated.
A composition-run coverage/verdict table for all ten ForkAudit targets in the format of Tables 9-10, with decisive witnesses, and an archive alias with manifest hash in Table 32.

The width-matched exact-cache arm (the 37.846 MiB point) actually executed with F1 and a paired interval, which would convert the 5.84x/3.41-point trade-off from a width-confounded observation into a matched-precision result.
An FP32-scale-metadata ablation of the full-prefix Q8 arm establishing that its 3.78-point F1 loss is a property of quantizing 40 layers rather than of BF16 scale rounding.

Release of the eleven unarchived deployment-stack components (panel runner, launcher, Store and deployment accountants, bootstrap and aggregation scripts, layer-policy search) so Table 4 becomes re-executable rather than only replayable.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: If a multi-document residency run shows the measured peak departs materially from S D + T(N) -- i.e. the terms are genuinely non-additive as the paper's own captions say -- the total-memory model and every crossover would have to be withdrawn, taking the paper to 2.

If the shared-versus-private transient difference (214.87 and 263.83 MiB) turns out not to be attributable to the audited sharing mechanism, the shared fit that sets the crossover is measuring an unrelated buffer effect and Table 1 loses its Q-CoMem line.

If the composition run's ten-target coverage cannot be exhibited per target and per slot, the abstract's and Conclusion's 'passing all ten contract targets' claim is unsupported and the packed-path ownership contribution collapses to a design argument.

If the full-prefix Q8 quality loss is shown to be a metadata-precision artifact, the '5.84x smaller at 3.41 points higher mean F1' comparison, its paired interval and the Section 5.4 ordering claim all fall.
Any further instance of a ratio reported against a reference arm other than the one named at the point of use.
review_limitations: PDF-only: I could not inspect source, evidence packages, per-item shards, or the supplementary research package, so all verification is limited to identities recomputable from printed numbers.

I could not check whether the archived per-repeat transient values support the medians in Table 5, nor whether the composition run's ten-target statuses re-derive as claimed; both are asserted and not tabulated.

The alternative crossovers I compute (6.73 documents at N = 1 under all-BF16 S; 4.30 at N = 8 under the private transient fit) use the paper's own printed fits and means and are therefore subject to the same 4-point fit uncertainty as the paper's values.
I did not evaluate novelty positioning or citation integrity in depth; that is outside my assigned lens, although Appendix G's attributions and the explicit XQuant delta appeared to me candid.
